title: Definite symmetric determinantal representation from Rayleigh differences
statement: Let $f\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$ be multiaffine in $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, with nonzero coefficient of $x_1\cdots x_n$. For indices $i,j$, let $\Delta_{ij}(f)$ denote the corresponding Rayleigh difference. **Definite symmetric determinantal representation conjecture.** Some power of $f$ has a definite real symmetric determinantal representation if and only if, for all $i,j$, $\Delta_{ij}(f)$ is a sum of squares in $\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$. This is presented as a hoped-for partial converse to a known result relating definite determinantal representations to sums of squares; its resolution is not given in the source.
source_name: Abeer Al Ahmadieh and Cynthia Vinzant, “Determinantal representations and the image of the principal minor map”, arXiv:2205.05267 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05267

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2022). “This conjecture was resolved by Oeding .”
